results.status: measured on a SIMULATED stream: PUBLIC freMTPL2 held-out policies with SYNTHETIC injected drift; indicators read from the latest results files
results.description: Continuous monitoring demonstration (Phase 6 B): input drift (PSI per feature), score drift (PSI of the predicted frequency), calibration drift (observed/predicted claims with an exact Poisson interval, ECE of P(claim > 0)) of a Poisson GLM, validated on SIMULATED streams; extraction, agent and reviewer indicators read from results files.

rule.rationale: The same bands as risk/stability.py and the model cards (stable < 0.10 <= moderate shift <= 0.25 < significant shift). A common industry rule of thumb, not a statistical test.
Same bands as the input PSI, so one scale reads every PSI in the report.

calibration_ratio.rationale: A +/-10% tolerance on the claim level is a round pricing tolerance. "warn" when the point estimate leaves the band; "alert" only when the whole 95% interval lies outside it, so the random noise of one window should rarely alert (the false alert rate actually measured is in the results). Below 50 predicted claims the check reports insufficient_data instead of a level.

rule.rationale: Equal-count bins, because most policies have no claim and equal-width bins would put almost every policy in the first bin. With 5,000 policies per window a bin holds 500 policies at a claim share of a few percent, so binomial noise alone keeps the ECE of every window above zero; the warn and alert levels were set above the size that noise was expected to have (the ECE of every demonstration window is in the results).

citation_support_rate.rationale: Share of extracted values whose cited page prints the value (results/docintel_metrics.json rules.citations.supported_all_values). One unsupported citation in 100 is the alert level.

ocr_page_share.rationale: Share of pages with no text layer that had to be read by OCR (the OCR fallback). Field accuracy is lower on scanned pages, so a growing share is an early warning about the input mix.

low_confidence_field_share.rationale: Share of extracted fields below the extractor's confidence cut. Kept so the rule exists when the metric does; results/docintel_metrics.json has no field-confidence metric today.

required_escalations_escalated.rationale: Every case that must reach a senior human (sanctions potential match, detected injection, policy referral) must be escalated; anything below 100% is a breach (results/agent_metrics.json).

unsupported_claim_rate.rationale: Share of memo claims with no supporting citation. Needs an LLM run; not measured in this checkout.

override_rate.rationale: Share of reviewed decisions where the reviewer overrode the recommendation, read from the "feedback" section of results/governance_metrics.json (SIMULATED reviewer decisions). A high rate says reviewers often disagree with the system.

limitations: freMTPL2 has no date or policy-year field, so no real stream of new business and no out-of-time split exist. Windows are random draws from the held-out split and every drift is INJECTED (SYNTHETIC scenarios).
All streams draw from one held-out pool of policies, so they are not independent samples of the world; the bootstrap intervals describe stream-to-stream variation for this pool and this model.
A window is an independent random draw (without replacement inside the window), so a policy can appear in two windows of one stream.
Outcomes are assumed known at the end of each window (no claim reporting lag, no IBNR); a real book sees claims months later, which adds that lag to every calibration detection delay.
Thresholds are design choices (config/monitoring.yaml), not fitted limits. The detection results hold for these scenarios, this window size and this model only.
The extraction, agent and reviewer indicators are single values read from the latest results files, not a stream; they cannot show drift over time.
Demonstration only: not a production monitoring system and not a compliance programme. Whether and how any monitoring expectation applies depends on the institution and its risk profile.

rows.title: Credit PD model (LightGBM, Lending Club) test AUC, lower bound of the 95% bootstrap CI
rows.why_critical: Discrimination of the probability-of-default model that ranks credit applicants. The lower CI bound is gated, not the point estimate, so a release must keep the conservative end of the interval. The tolerance equals the minimum AUC gain the model-selection rule treats as material (credit.results.model_selection.min_auc_gain).
rows.note: The paths name LightGBM, the model the selection rule chose. The precondition pins that choice to a fixed value rather than to the baseline's, so a flip still fails after a reviewed baseline update: the row must then be pointed at the newly chosen model's paths and this value changed with it.

rows.title: Claim-frequency model (preferred LightGBM, freMTPL2) test mean Poisson deviance, upper bound of the 95% CI
rows.why_critical: Fit of the claim-frequency model that drives the expected-loss price. Deviance is lower-is-better, so the upper CI bound is gated. The tolerance is below the LightGBM-over-GLM deviance gain recorded on the same test split (insurance_frequency.results.test_metrics.lgbm_minus_glm), so a regression that erases most of the reason for preferring LightGBM blocks a release.
rows.note: The paths name the preferred model, LightGBM (preferred_model.name = lgbm); the precondition fails the row when another model is preferred (see credit_auc_ci_low for why the value is fixed). freMTPL2 has no date field, so this is a random-split test, not an out-of-time test.

notes: The gate reads numbers other scripts wrote to results/*.json and recomputes none of them. They come from evaluations on SYNTHETIC data (packets, applications, founder scenarios) and on public data (Lending Club, freMTPL2); none is a production measurement.
NOT_MEASURED rows are listed, never counted as passing: the metric has no value in the current results or the baseline (for example the LLM-dependent metrics, because no LLM was run).

Injection: action-level containment (injected text cannot make the agent take a decision) is enforced by tests/security/test_containment.py in the CI test job, which the release-gate job waits for; that is a test result, not an attack success rate. The per-layer attack success rates are gated only when results/injection_metrics.json exists; they hold for the frozen payload set only.

Preconditions (config/release_gate.yaml) are checked before a measured number is compared: a partial injection run, an agent run on the first N applications, a dev-split or subset document run, another evaluation set than the baseline's, or a chosen model other than the one a row's paths name makes the row FAIL instead of being compared with the full reviewed baseline.

git_dirty warnings do not fail the gate today: most committed results files were written from a working tree with uncommitted changes. They are listed so the files can be regenerated at a clean commit.
STALE (evidence measured on another prompt, corpus or model than HEAD, docs/innovations.md S3) is not checked: this gate recomputes no provenance hash.
This is a demonstration of a release gate, not a compliance programme; whether such a gate is adequate depends on the institution and its risk profile.
